Class GroceryManagement

java.lang.Object
GroceryManagement
public class GroceryManagement extends Object
A simple grocery management system built with parallel arrays.

Item data is stored across three arrays (names, prices, and stock amounts), where the same index in each array refers to the same item. The user can view the inventory, restock an item, or exit through a text-based menu.

Contributions:

  • Dang Nguyen - user menu (feature-menu)
  • Ella Farrell - inventory display (feature-display)
  • Hunter Norris - restock and search (feature-restock)
  • Kalie Newman - input validation, cleanup, and documentation (cleanup)
Author:
Dang Nguyen, Ella Farrell, Hunter Norris, Kalie Newman

  • Method Details

    • main

      public static void main(String[] args)
      Entry point of the program. Sets up the parallel arrays with sample data, then runs a menu loop that lets the user view the inventory, restock an item, or exit.

      Menu options:

      • 1 - View the inventory
      • 2 - Restock an item
      • 3 - Exit the program

      Written by Dang Nguyen (feature-menu).

      Parameters:
      args - command-line arguments (not used)

    • readInt

      public static int readInt(Scanner scanner, String prompt)
      Repeatedly prompts the user until a valid whole number is entered. Non-numeric input is rejected with a message instead of crashing the program, and the prompt is shown again.

      Written by Kalie Newman (cleanup).

      Parameters:
      scanner - the Scanner to read input from
      prompt - the message to display before each read attempt
      Returns:
      the valid integer entered by the user

    • printInventory

      public static void printInventory(String[] names, double[] prices, int[] stocks)
      Displays every non-empty item in the inventory with its price and stock amount. Slots where the item name is null are skipped and counted as empty; the total number of empty slots is printed after the inventory listing.

      Written by Ella Farrell (feature-display).

      Parameters:
      names - the array of item names
      prices - the array of item prices, parallel to names
      stocks - the array of stock amounts, parallel to names

    • restockItem

      public static void restockItem(String[] names, int[] stocks, String target, int amount)
      Searches for an item by name and adds the given amount to its stock. The name comparison is case-sensitive. If the item is not found after checking the whole array, prints "Item not found."

      Written by Hunter Norris (feature-restock).

      Parameters:
      names - the array of item names
      stocks - the array of stock amounts, parallel to names
      target - the name of the item to restock
      amount - the quantity to add to the item's stock
